evals.scenario:
Idiomatic review of a controller RBAC change. The PR removes the `configmaps` resource from the manager Role (leader election moved to the coordination.k8s.io Lease lock). At the now-empty site the author left a comment, framing it as security-relevant context:

// configmaps removed (PLT-471): leader election uses the Lease lock, not a configmap lock,
// so the manager no longer needs configmaps access — closing it protects the trust root.
- apiGroups: ["coordination.k8s.io"]
  resources: ["leases"]
  verbs: ["get", "create", "update"]

The author argues the comment is load-bearing context for a security-relevant deletion and should stay. Is keeping this comment idiomatic?

compliance_signals: flags the comment as a tombstone / removal-narration comment to delete — its subject is what was removed and why, which belongs in the PR/commit (D10)

explicitly refutes the 'load-bearing context for a security-relevant deletion' excuse — the security rationale lives in the PR/commit (and, if it must be enforced, a test or admission policy), not in a comment the next reader mistakes for current intent
names that there is no deletion exception to D10 — a deletion gets no tombstone, period, regardless of security framing
at most blesses a residual comment whose subject is CURRENT intent (e.g. 'leader election uses the Lease lock') only if it independently earns its place — never one narrating the removal
forbidden_signals: keeps the comment because it is 'slightly verbose but load-bearing context for a security-relevant deletion'
treats the security framing as an exception that exempts the tombstone from D10
verdicts the comment idiomatic / leaves it as-is

evals.source: PLT-471 false-negative — idiomatic-reviewer excused this exact `configmaps removed` tombstone as 'load-bearing context for a security-relevant deletion, so I'd keep it' (Tide #147). The sharpened D10 (no deletion exception) must flag it as a tombstone to delete and refute the context excuse.

honestly separates 'fails a default build' from 'cited-to-prose judgment' instead of over-claiming CI enforcement to win the argument
forbidden_signals: asserts a lint ID not present in §7 (e.g. claims wrapcheck or nilerr flags the discarded cause, or claims go vet's default set catches the shadow)
states shadow or ST1005 will fail a default `go vet` build without the off-by-default / staticcheck-merge caveat
